ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy bade4db5c2e0 (2026-04-28T14:14:11Z) modified LogBuffer.java and application.properties, inadvertently setting flush_threshold=DISABLED and max_buffer_entries=UNBOUNDED for the async log buffer in ad-service. Under high ad request throughput (>300 rps), every GetAds call appends structured log entries to an in-memory ArrayList in LogBuffer.append() (line 218) that is never flushed, causing unbounded heap growth. This triggers progressive GC pressure (gc_overhead_pct rising from 12% to 41%+) and ultimately OOMKill (exit code 137) within ~2 minutes of startup under load. The crash loop repeats on every pod restart because the misconfiguration is baked into the deployed artifact.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately roll back ad-service to the previous stable deploy (sha: c789fc89a688) using `kubectl set image deployment/ad-service ad-service=ad-service:c789fc89a688` to break the OOMKill crash loop. 2. Delete the current crashing pod to force clean restart: `kubectl delete pod ad-service-7d8f9b-xkqpl`. 3. In the code, fix LogBuffer.java to re-enable flush_threshold (e.g., flush every 1000 entries or every 5 seconds) and cap max_buffer_entries to a safe limit (e.g., 10000) to prevent unbounded growth. 4. Restore the correct application.properties values: `log.buffer.flush_threshold=1000` and `log.buffer.max_entries=10000`. 5. Cut a hotfix release, validate in staging under load, and redeploy. 6. Add a heap usage alert at 70% and a JVM GC overhead alert at >20% to catch regression early.
